name: sbml-spatial-hybrid
title: The hybrid model described in SBML Spatial, run on both solvers
question:
Can a PDE/particle hybrid be described in SBML Spatial, with each species' representation
(continuous or particle) as a VCell annotation, and run unchanged from that SBML on both
the native VCell solver and the co-simulation?
hypothesis:
The SBML carries everything the model needs (geometry, species, diffusion, initial
conditions, mass-action reactions, representations), so a run from the SBML reproduces the
run from the original model exactly, seed for seed, on each solver.
objective:
The A3 two-way exchange (11×11×3 slab, 10×10×1 µm; A_p → B at 1 s⁻¹, B → A_p at
0.5 s⁻¹·[B]; B₀ = 0.2 µM; dt = 0.01; 2 s; 8 seeds). `to_sbml` writes it to SBML Spatial
(A particle, B continuous); it is then run four ways:
- native from the original model (`to_biomodel` VCML) and native from the SBML (VCell's SBML
  import → libvcell → vcell-fvsolver);
- co-sim from the Python `HybridModel` and co-sim from `from_sbml`.
description:
Phase 6 (docs/PLAN.md). The representation annotation and its import/export are in VCell
(virtualcell/vcell#2175); libvcell adds `vcml_convert_units` (virtualcell/libvcell#26) and
pyvcell `load_sbml_str(..., unit_system="vcell")` (virtualcell/pyvcell#63; VCell imports SBML in the SBML's own units). Needs those builds:
`run.py` uses `run_native(..., sbml=...)` and `from_sbml`.

Found on the way: VCell's spatial stochastic math is only consistent in VCell's default
units. A hybrid imported in VCell's SBML units (dm, µmol, l) gave Smoldyn a world in dm with
creation rates per µm³, so field-driven creation produced almost nothing. VCell's SBML import
now converts such models to its default units.

behavior_tests.name: model-round-trips-exactly
behavior_tests.description: from_sbml(to_sbml(model)) equals the original HybridModel (grid, species, representations, reactions).

provenance.note: The SBML carries every model quantity; rate constants are recovered exactly from VCell's mass-action rate.

behavior_tests.name: cosim-from-sbml-is-identical
behavior_tests.description: The co-simulation from the SBML reproduces the co-simulation from the original model seed for seed.

behavior_tests.name: native-from-sbml-is-identical
behavior_tests.description: The native VCell run from the SBML reproduces the native run from the original VCML seed for seed.

provenance.note: VCell's SBML import yields math equivalent to the original's (SBMLSpatialHybridTest), so the solver input is the same.

canonical_runs.name: default
canonical_runs.label: A3 two-way exchange from SBML Spatial: 8 seeds × (native, co-sim) × (original, SBML)

conclusion:
Results (results/metrics.json, 2026-10-08; released stack: vcell-fvsolver 0.11.1, libvcell 0.0.19, pyvcell 0.4.2):
- **The model round-trips exactly** through SBML Spatial, including the representations and
  all rate constants.
- **Each solver reproduces itself from the SBML, seed for seed:** co-sim and native runs from
  the SBML are bit-identical to the runs from the original model.
- **Across solvers (rerun 2026-10-08 on the released vcell-fvsolver 0.11.1, which carries
  #32-#34):** native and co-sim agree (max |z| 1.45 for A, 1.14 for B; native A ends at 3827 vs
  3845) and native conserves A + B to +0.12%. On 0.10.7, native over-created at boundary nodes
  (virtualcell/vcell-fvsolver#24): A ended at 2.3× the co-sim's (|z| 135) and A + B grew 76%.
